name: Spark
scope: A person with INTERMEDIATE proficiency level in Spark as a competency should be able to design, build, debug and operate Spark applications that exploit RDD, DataFrame and Dataset APIs while fully understanding driver–executor roles, stages, tasks, shuffles, Tungsten whole-stage code-gen, Catalyst logical→physical plans and memory segments across standalone, YARN and Kubernetes clusters. They fluently code in Scala or PySpark (can read Java), author UDFs, apply narrow/wide transformations, window functions, aggregations, all join types, broadcast variables, accumulators, map-side joins, schema evolution tactics and interpret explain() plans for optimisation. They integrate with Parquet, ORC, Avro, CSV, JSON, Text, Delta, Iceberg and Hudi in Snappy/ZSTD/GZIP/LZ4, manage Hive/Glue/Unity Catalog metastores, implement partitioning, bucketing, CDC ingest, compaction and vacuum, and connect to Kafka, Kinesis, Pulsar, JDBC, Cassandra, HBase, MongoDB, S3, ADLS, GCS or REST with Kerberos/SASL/OAuth. They architect modular ETL/ELT layers, idempotent reprocessing and data contracts, orchestrated by Airflow, Oozie, Dagster, Prefect, Azure Data Factory or Databricks Jobs with SLAs, retries and backfills. They tune performance via executor/driver sizing, GC, Kryo, off-heap, coalesce/repartition, dynamic partition overwrites, salting, skew fixes, shuffle compression, broadcast thresholds, AQE and dynamic join reordering while reading Spark UI, event logs, Prometheus, Datadog or Ganglia metrics. They build Structured Streaming apps with fixed/once/continuous triggers, watermarks, stateful aggregations, RocksDB state store, streaming joins, exactly-once Kafka sinks, backpressure control and mini-batch latency optimisation. They employ MLlib pipelines (Transformers, Estimators, CrossValidator, TrainValidationSplit), common algorithms (GBDT, logistic regression, K-means), persist models, export to MLeap/ONNX and know GraphX Pregel, PageRank and connected components with optional Horovod integration. They enforce code quality using scalatest or pytest, run local/mini-cluster tests in CI (GitHub Actions, Jenkins, Azure DevOps), apply data quality checks via Deequ or Great Expectations, maintain golden datasets and lineage via Atlas/OpenLineage. They secure workloads with TLS, Kerberos, LDAP, OAuth2/OIDC, Ranger/Atlas/Unity Catalog row/column masking, at-rest encryption and manage audit logs and key rotation impacts on checkpoints. They package with sbt, Maven, Gradle, pip or conda, create shaded JARs, resolve dependency conflicts, develop in IntelliJ, VS Code, Jupyter or Databricks notebooks, debug locally or via spark-submit and version with GitFlow or trunk-based branching. Finally, they participate in agile sprints, conduct code reviews, write runbooks, uphold production SLAs, perform on-call triage and mentor juniors on Spark best practices.

INTERMEDIATE‐LEVEL SPARK COMPETENCY  
(≈ 3–5 years hands-on, full-time experience)

The following scope describes, in depth and breadth, everything an individual at INTERMEDIATE proficiency is expected to know, understand, build, operate, optimise, secure and govern when using Apache Spark in production.  The scope is purposely exhaustive, so that interview questions derived from it can probe any facet of the competency without leaving blind spots.

────────────────────────────────────────
1. Foundational Architecture & Execution Model
────────────────────────────────────────
• Internal abstractions  
  – Complete, working knowledge of Resilient Distributed Datasets (RDDs), DataFrames and Datasets, their lineage, immutability and serialization semantics.  
  – Awareness of the advantages, trade-offs and interoperability between the three APIs; ability to justify API choice for a given workload.  

• Logical → Physical plan compilation  
  – Understanding of Catalyst’s rule-based and cost-based optimisation phases, predicate push-down, constant folding, projection pruning and statistics gathering.  
  – Ability to interpret the explain()/query execution plan, locate expensive stages and correlate them to source code.  

• Execution components  
  – Driver, executor, task, stage, job, shuffle read/write, broadcast exchange, Tungsten’s whole-stage code generation and vectorised execution.  
  – Familiarity with Spark’s memory regions (storage, execution, user, reserved, off-heap) and spill-to-disk thresholds.  

• Cluster managers  
  – Ability to run jobs reliably on YARN, standalone and Kubernetes, with a deep understanding of how Spark is packaged, submitted, started, and monitored under each.  

────────────────────────────────────────
2. Development & API Mastery
────────────────────────────────────────
• Language fluency  
  – Expert-level fluency in at least one primary API (Scala or PySpark) and literate proficiency in the other, including UDF creation, typed Datasets (Scala) and vectorised pandas UDFs (Python).  
  – Familiarity with Java API; ability to read and debug mixed-language code bases.  

• Transformations & actions  
  – Complete coverage of narrow vs. wide transformations, custom partitioners, combineByKey/aggregateByKey, window functions, join types (inner, outer, semi, anti, skew, cross, self).  

• Columnar & SQL constructs  
  – Proficient use of Spark SQL syntax, DataFrame DSL, higher-order functions, complex data types (arrays, maps, structs), JSON handling, regex, conditional expressions, date-time APIs.  
  – Competence in schema evolution, schema merging, user-provided vs. inferred schemas, nullable handling, and schema enforcement via case classes or StructType definitions.  

• Side-data patterns  
  – Effective use of broadcast variables, accumulators, map-side joins, broadcast-hash joins vs. shuffle-hash/-sort-merge joins.  

• Error handling & fault tolerance  
  – Mastery of try/except constructs, retry patterns, idempotent transformations, job check-pointing, stage retries, speculative execution and lineage-based recomputation.  

────────────────────────────────────────
3. Data Sources, Formats & Storage
────────────────────────────────────────
• File formats & compression  
  – Operational skills with Parquet, ORC, Avro, CSV, JSON, Text, Delta, Iceberg, Hudi, along with Snappy, ZSTD, GZIP and LZ4 compression.  
  – Understanding of columnar vs. row-oriented implications, predicate push-down, statistics, bloom filters and partition pruning.  

• Catalogues & metastore integration  
  – Working knowledge of Hive Metastore, Glue, Unity Catalog or other metastore integrations, external vs. managed tables, table properties, transactional tables.  

• Incremental ingestion patterns  
  – Change Data Capture (CDC) capture/replay, schema evolution, late arriving data, small-file mitigation, compaction strategies and vacuum / retention settings.  

• Connectivity  
  – Reading/writing from Kafka, Kinesis, Pulsar, JDBC (RDBMS), NoSQL stores (Cassandra, HBase, MongoDB), cloud storage blobs (S3/ADLS/GCS), message queues and REST / microservice endpoints.  
  – Kerberos/SASL/OAuth token handling for secured sources.  

────────────────────────────────────────
4. Pipeline Design & Orchestration
────────────────────────────────────────
• Modular ETL/ELT design  
  – Layered data-engineering patterns (raw → cleansed → curated → serving), data contracts, schema registries, partitioning/granularity decisions.  

• Workflow orchestration  
  – Building DAG-driven pipelines using Airflow, Oozie, Dagster, Prefect, Azure Data Factory or Databricks Jobs; understanding of retries, SLAs, backfill and promotion between environments.  

• Idempotency & reprocessing  
  – Use of checkpointing, watermarking, deduplication techniques and exactly-once semantics at micro-batch level (Structured Streaming).  

────────────────────────────────────────
5. Performance Tuning & Resource Optimisation
────────────────────────────────────────
• Partitioning  
  – Determining optimal file size, input vs. output partition counts, coalesce vs. repartition, dynamic partition overwrites, bucketing, salting for data-skew mitigation.  

• Memory & compute sizing  
  – Executor sizing heuristics, driver memory vs. executor memory, cores vs. tasks, GC tuning, off-heap memory, Kryo vs. Java serialization, broadcast threshold tuning.  

• Shuffle reduction strategies  
  – Avoiding wide dependencies, pushdown filters, local vs. clustered shuffles, shuffle compression, shuffle service tuning, adaptive query execution (AQE) and dynamic join reordering.  

• Spark UI & metrics  
  – Navigating stages, tasks, storage, SQL tabs; using event logs, speculative metrics, structured-streaming metrics, Ganglia/Prometheus/Datadog integrations; root-cause analysis of slow tasks.  

────────────────────────────────────────
6. Structured Streaming & Real-Time Processing
────────────────────────────────────────
• Triggering & micro-batch model  
  – fixed-interval, once, continuous triggers; watermarking, event-time vs. processing-time choices, late data handling, state store management, state TTL.  

• Sources & sinks  
  – Kafka, Kinesis, Pulsar, socket, file streams, RateSource, foreachBatch sink, memory sink, console sink, Kafka exactly-once semantics with transactions.  

• Checkpointing & fault tolerance  
  – Stateful streaming aggregations, RocksDB state management (for large states), backpressure handling, streaming join types and limitations.  

• End-to-end latency optimisation  
  – Mini-batch size vs. throughput, serialization overhead, shuffle in streaming, streaming joins across watermarks, handling backfills.  

────────────────────────────────────────
7. Machine Learning & Graph Processing (Foundational)
────────────────────────────────────────
• MLlib pipeline APIs  
  – Transformers, estimators, fit/transform, pipeline persistence; feature transformers (VectorAssembler, StringIndexer, OneHotEncoder, HashingTF), evaluators, ML persistence.  
  – Training and deploying moderate-scale models (GBDT, logistic regression, K-means) in Spark; hyper-parameter tuning with CrossValidator and TrainValidationSplit.  

• GraphX fundamentals  
  – Graph abstraction, Pregel API, message passing, connected components, page rank, relationship to datasets/dataframes.  

• Integration with external ML platforms  
  – Saving feature vectors to Parquet/Delta for downstream systems, exporting to MLeap/ONNX, using Horovod or distributed Deep Learning frameworks (high-level familiarity).  

────────────────────────────────────────
8. Quality Engineering & Governance
────────────────────────────────────────
• Code quality  
  – Unit & integration testing with scalatest/pytest, Spark local mode vs. mini-clusters, golden data sets; continuous integration pipelines (GitHub Actions, Jenkins, Azure DevOps).  

• Data quality  
  – Column-level constraints, null/unique checks, statistical drift detection, library usage (Deequ, Great Expectations), quarantine patterns for defective records.  

• Documentation & reproducibility  
  – Automatic notebook/job documentation, schema history management, reproducible builds via sbt/maven/poetry; semantic versioning of data schemas and pipeline code.  

────────────────────────────────────────
9. Security, Compliance & Governance
────────────────────────────────────────
• Authentication & authorisation  
  – Kerberos, LDAP, OAuth2/OIDC, integration with Ranger/Atlas/UnityCatalog; fine-grained table/column masking, row-level security.  

• Encryption  
  – TLS between driver ↔ executor ↔ shuffle service, SSL for data sources, at-rest encryption via HDFS, S3, ADLS; key-rotation implications on checkpoints.  

• Auditing & lineage  
  – Emitting audit events, integrating with Atlas/OpenLineage, capturing execution context, lineage tags in Delta/iceberg, differential & impact analysis.  

────────────────────────────────────────
10. Tooling, IDEs & Packaging
────────────────────────────────────────
• Build tooling  
  – sbt, maven, gradle, pip/conda; shaded JAR creation, dependency management, resolving conflicts through exclusion rules or relocation.  

• IDEs & notebooks  
  – IntelliJ + Scala plugin, Visual Studio Code + Metals/Jupyter, Databricks notebooks, Zeppelin; debugging in local/spark-submit/remote modes.  

• Version control & branching  
  – GitFlow / trunk-based workflows, submodule management for shared libraries, tagging releases, release notes.  

────────────────────────────────────────
11. Collaboration & Delivery Outcomes
────────────────────────────────────────
• Agile / DevOps integration  
  – Participating in sprint planning, translating user stories to Spark workloads, demonstrating deliverables, maintaining production runbooks and SLAs.  

• Mentoring & knowledge transfer  
  – On-boarding juniors on Spark basics, conducting code reviews, authoring best-practice wikis, promoting performance and cost-awareness culture.  

• Production ownership  
  – 24×7 on-call rotation readiness, incident triage, root-cause analysis, permanent fixes, post-mortems and capacity planning for future workload growth.  

────────────────────────────────────────
Summary of Expected Deliverables for an INTERMEDIATE Practitioner
────────────────────────────────────────
• Build and deploy batch or micro-batch pipelines that process 10s of TB, complete in SLA, are cost-aware, and are observably robust.  
• Diagnose and remediate common performance pathologies: data skew, small files, shuffle explosions, sub-optimal joins, memory pressure.  
• Implement data quality and governance controls so that downstream consumers can trust, trace and reuse the outputs.  
• Integrate Spark jobs seamlessly into larger data platforms (streaming, ML, BI, CDC pipelines) and automate their promotion through dev → test → prod.  
• Keep production clusters healthy, secure and compliant, while iterating on features at sprint cadence.  

Everything above constitutes the full scope against which interview questions for INTERMEDIATE Apache Spark proficiency should be devised.
